identity: Film director and designer · United States · 1912–1988
title: Ray Eames's birth chart
metaDescription: Ray Eames's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 23.5° Sagittarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the ten placements whose signs are settled stand in Sagittarius — the Sun, Mercury, Mars and Jupiter. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At the noon reference the Sun sits 23.5° into Sagittarius — the third decan, which the old scheme hands to the Sun. Same sign, different decan, different chart.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 9.2° Sagittarius; Venus stands at 3.5° Aquarius; Mars stands at 11.1° Sagittarius. The tradition reads thought that arrives already in motion from Mercury, attraction that begins as conversation from Venus, effort spent in bursts and openings from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The tightest geometry in the chart puts Mercury in the same degree of the zodiac from Mars, 2.0° off exact. The tradition stops reading a conjunction as two things. It is one appetite with two names, and it moves together or not at all. Behind it, Venus conjunction Uranus at 2.2°, and the Sun conjunction Jupiter at 2.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: No closed figure — no grand trine, t-square, or grand cross — holds among the day-stable angles. The chart distributes its tension pair by pair rather than through one standing structure.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks two placements here. Mercury in Sagittarius at 9.2° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Jupiter in Sagittarius at 25.9° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Balance, counted honestly across the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: elements fire 4, air 3, water 2, earth 1; modalities mutable 6, fixed 3, cardinal 1. Fire weights a chart toward initiative — starting, asserting, spending energy to find out what happens. Mercury, Saturn, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Pisces for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 11.8° between midnight and midnight. The missing clock moves the Moon by half a sign at most here, and the boundary was never close. At the noon reference it stands at 12.6°.
